title: quant-profile-sanity-prober-and-layerwise-noise-clamp-for-e4m3-e5m2
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Safely enable FP8 (E4M3/E5M2) quantization profiles for a selected set of Hopper-backed production models by building a reproducible "prober" harness and a new layerwise noise-clamp calibration stage. This ticket implements the calibration pipeline glue, the prober CI checks, and canary gating rules; it also codifies deterministic rollback criteria and an operational runbook.

Background: Previous FP8 attempts showed stable throughput improvements but intermittent quality regressions on corner prompts (in particular long instruction tokens and low-frequency token predictions). We need a reproducible activation mechanism that: (1) identifies fragile layers per model, (2) reduces quantization-induced noise via per-layer clamps and proportional activation, and (3) surfaces actionable telemetry for safe rollout.

Approach: 
- Add a "quant-prober" job that runs shadow FP8 inference across curated golden slices (diverse prompt families and long-tail examples) and compares logits/LL to FP16 baseline. Prober runs as part of pre-rollout CI and nightly canaries.
- Implement layerwise noise-clamp: compute per-layer scale and clamp thresholds during calibration; during inference apply soft-hysteresis clamping where quantized activations outside calibrated band are attenuated rather than zeroed.
- Proportional activation heuristic: allow partial FP8 activation per-shard and per-layer (0-100%) so we can ramp activation based on observed drift score.
- Telemetry: add new metrics (slice-level KL, top-k swap rate, per-layer activation ratio, noisy-layer heatmap) and dashboard panels; wire alerts to regression thresholds.
- Stability fixes: guard against KV-cache corruption by validating cache fingerprints post-FP8 path; add deterministic fallback path to FP16 for requests with fingerprint mismatches.

Acceptance criteria: 
1) Quant-prober runs in CI and produces a reproducible report that includes: per-slice KL, per-layer noise histogram, and delta-latency.
2) Nightly canary job executes on 1% of traffic for two models with shadow FP8 active; no slice in the golden set exceeds KL>0.015 or top-1 swap rate >0.8% for 72 hours.
3) Layerwise noise-clamp reduces worst-case token LL drop by >=40% on our long-tail slice vs naive FP8 baseline.
4) Rollout policy implemented: progressive activation 0->10->25->50->100 with automated rollback triggers tied to slice-level alerts.
5) Runbook documented and reviewed by SRE/Trust.

Out-of-scope: global INT8 rollout, model re-training, hardware kernel changes.

Test plan and data: 
- Golden set: s3://redwood-quant/gold-slices/2026-02-v2 (diverse domains, 35k examples).
- CI prober: github action that runs on PRs touching runtime quant code.
- Canary: rolling shadow on dedicated canary pool; traffic gating implemented in serving router.

Operational notes: 
- If drift detector triggers >3 contiguous slices, the activation is stepped down and customers on dedicated pools are notified via incident channel.
- Escalation path in runbook: on-call -> quant infra -> model owner -> customer success.

Risks and mitigation: 
- Risk: False positives on KL metric due to tokenization differences. Mitigation: normalize tokenization and report token-aligned KL.
- Risk: Latency regression at 100% activation for long sequences. Mitigation: include latency SLO checks in prober and stage CPU-level profiling.

Notes about compatibility: Prober is model-agnostic but calibration artifacts are stored per-model version. Calibration artifacts are tagged with model, model_version, quant_profile and a calibration-seed hash.
